questions.question: 🦅 Sami receives a 6-year-old child with a loose baby tooth. He says: 'Let's extract it right away!' 🐆 Mina replies: 'Not so fast!' What is the eruption sequence of primary teeth?
options: Central incisors (6-10 months), lateral incisors (8-12 months), first molars (12-18 months), canines (16-22 months), second molars (24-30 months)
All baby teeth come out at the same time
questions.explanation: 🦅 Sami explains: 'The eruption sequence is well established. Central incisors are first, followed by laterals, molars, canines, and second molars.' 🐆 Mina: 'Sami, you know your dental development!'

questions.question: 🐆 Mina, examining a 4-year-old child, says: 'He has early childhood caries.' 🦅 Sami replies: 'It's not serious, they're just baby teeth!' Why are caries in baby teeth concerning?
options: They can affect the germs of permanent teeth and cause space problems
They disappear with the baby teeth
questions.explanation: 🐆 Mina explains: 'Caries in baby teeth can reach the germs of permanent teeth and compromise space for eruption.' 🦅 Sami: 'Fine, we'll treat it, but it's long...'

questions.question: 🦅 Sami, seeing a deep cavity on a baby tooth, says: 'We need to extract!' 🐆 Mina replies: 'And what about pulpotomy?' What is a pulpotomy?
options: Partial removal of the coronal pulp to preserve the baby tooth
Placing a crown without pulpal treatment
questions.explanation: 🦅 Sami explains: 'Pulpotomy is a conservative treatment that preserves the baby tooth and its space.' 🐆 Mina: 'Sami, you're becoming conservative!'

questions.question: 🐆 Mina, seeing an 8-year-old child with permanent teeth, says: 'We need to seal the pits and fissures.' 🦅 Sami replies: 'Useless, brushing is enough.' What is pit and fissure sealant?
options: A resin applied to occlusal surfaces to prevent caries
questions.explanation: 🐆 Mina explains: 'Pit and fissure sealants are an effective preventive measure against occlusal caries.' 🦅 Sami: 'I prefer brushing, but I admit you're right.'

questions.question: 🦅 Sami, examining a 3-year-old child, says: 'He has a bad occlusion.' 🐆 Mina replies: 'That's normal at this age!' What is primary occlusion?
options: The occlusion of baby teeth, with overjet and crossbite often physiological
questions.explanation: 🦅 Sami explains: 'Primary occlusion has its own characteristics. A crossbite can be physiological.' 🐆 Mina: 'Sami, you're really up to date!'

questions.question: 🐆 Mina, seeing a child with decayed baby teeth, says: 'We need to restore them.' 🦅 Sami replies: 'No, extraction!' Which approach is preferable?
options: Restoration preserves space and function until permanent teeth erupt
questions.explanation: 🐆 Mina explains: 'Restoring baby teeth is important to maintain space and function.' 🦅 Sami: 'I prefer extraction for speed, but you're right.'

questions.question: 🦅 Sami, seeing a 5-year-old child with an impacted tooth, says: 'It's a baby tooth, let's extract!' 🐆 Mina replies: 'Not so fast!' Why can an impacted baby tooth be concerning?
options: It can cause ankylosis or affect the eruption of the permanent tooth
It will come out on its own
questions.explanation: 🦅 Sami explains: 'An impacted or ankylosed baby tooth can disrupt the eruption of the permanent tooth.' 🐆 Mina: 'Sami, you're making progress!'

questions.question: 🐆 Mina, examining a 7-year-old child, says: 'The first permanent molars have erupted.' 🦅 Sami replies: 'That's not important.' Why are the first permanent molars crucial?
options: They are the key to occlusion and guide the eruption of other teeth
They fall out like baby teeth
questions.explanation: 🐆 Mina explains: 'The 6-year molars (first permanent molars) are the pillars of occlusion.' 🦅 Sami: 'I didn't know, thank you Mina!'

questions.question: 🦅 Sami, seeing a child with a thumb-sucking habit, says: 'It's not serious.' 🐆 Mina replies: 'Yes, it can have consequences!' What are the consequences of prolonged thumb-sucking?
options: Anterior open bite, arch deformation, retrognathia
questions.explanation: 🦅 Sami explains: 'Prolonged thumb-sucking can cause dentofacial deformations.' 🐆 Mina: 'Sami, you know the subject well!'

questions.question: 🐆 Mina, seeing a child with geographic tongue, says: 'It's benign.' 🦅 Sami replies: 'I don't know that.' What is geographic tongue?
options: A benign condition with depapillated areas on the tongue
questions.explanation: 🐆 Mina explains: 'Geographic tongue is a benign and asymptomatic condition.' 🦅 Sami: 'I'll remember for next time!'

questions.question: 🦅 Sami, seeing a 4-year-old child with white spots on teeth, says: 'It's a cavity!' 🐆 Mina replies: 'Not necessarily, it could be fluorosis.' What is dental fluorosis?
options: Hypomineralization of enamel due to excess fluoride during development
questions.explanation: 🦅 Sami explains: 'Fluorosis is an enamel alteration linked to excess fluoride.' 🐆 Mina: 'Sami, you are well informed!'

questions.question: 🐆 Mina, examining a 6-year-old child, says: 'He has a cavity between the teeth.' 🦅 Sami replies: 'I don't see anything.' How to detect an interproximal cavity?
questions.explanation: 🐆 Mina explains: 'Interproximal caries are often only visible on X-rays.' 🦅 Sami: 'I'll prescribe X-rays next time.'

questions.question: 🦅 Sami, seeing a child with a loose baby tooth, says: 'Let's extract.' 🐆 Mina replies: 'And if it's a permanent tooth?' How to differentiate a baby tooth from a permanent tooth?
options: Baby teeth are whiter, smaller, and have finer roots
questions.explanation: 🦅 Sami explains: 'Baby teeth have distinctive characteristics: bluish-white color, smaller size, thin roots.' 🐆 Mina: 'Sami, you're an expert!'

questions.question: 🐆 Mina, seeing a child with gingivitis, says: 'It's linked to plaque.' 🦅 Sami replies: 'No, it's hormonal.' What is the main cause of gingivitis in children?
questions.explanation: 🐆 Mina explains: 'Dental plaque is the main cause of gingivitis in children.' 🦅 Sami: 'Fine, I'll teach him how to brush.'

questions.question: 🦅 Sami, examining a 2-year-old child, says: 'He has early childhood caries.' 🐆 Mina asks: 'What are the risk factors?'
options: Nighttime bottle-feeding, frequent sugary diet, insufficient hygiene
questions.explanation: 🦅 Sami explains: 'Risk factors are multiple and often linked to dietary habits.' 🐆 Mina: 'Sami, you know your subject!'

questions.question: 🐆 Mina, seeing a child with a fractured baby tooth, says: 'We need to assess the urgency.' 🦅 Sami replies: 'Let's extract.' What to do in case of a baby tooth fracture?
options: Radiological evaluation to check pulpal or root involvement
questions.explanation: 🐆 Mina explains: 'An X-ray is necessary to evaluate the extent of the fracture.' 🦅 Sami: 'Fine, we'll do an X-ray first.'

questions.question: 🦅 Sami, seeing a child with a tongue bite, says: 'It's not serious.' 🐆 Mina replies: 'It can be linked to a malocclusion.' What is the most frequent cause?
questions.explanation: 🦅 Sami explains: 'Tongue bites are often linked to habits or malocclusions.' 🐆 Mina: 'Sami, you're on fire today!'

questions.question: 🐆 Mina, examining a 9-year-old child, says: 'He has permanent teeth with spots.' 🦅 Sami replies: 'It's a cavity.' What is amelogenesis imperfecta?
options: A genetic enamel anomaly causing fragile and discolored teeth
questions.explanation: 🐆 Mina explains: 'Amelogenesis imperfecta is a rare genetic pathology.' 🦅 Sami: 'I didn't know, thank you Mina!'

questions.question: 🦅 Sami, seeing a child with a persistent baby tooth, says: 'Let's extract.' 🐆 Mina replies: 'And if the permanent tooth is absent?' What to do in case of a persistent baby tooth?
options: X-ray to check the presence of the permanent tooth
questions.explanation: 🦅 Sami explains: 'We must first check if the permanent tooth exists or not.' 🐆 Mina: 'Sami, you are really cautious!'

questions.question: 🐆 Mina, seeing a child with an abscess on a baby tooth, says: 'We need to treat or extract.' 🦅 Sami replies: 'No, antibiotics.' What is a dental abscess in children?
options: A localized infection at the apex or furcation of the tooth
questions.explanation: 🐆 Mina explains: 'The abscess requires local treatment (pulpotomy or extraction) and sometimes antibiotics.' 🦅 Sami: 'Fine, we'll treat locally.'

questions.question: 🦅 Sami, seeing a child with a baby crown, says: 'Why put a crown on a baby tooth?' 🐆 Mina replies: 'To preserve the tooth and the space.' What are the advantages of pediatric crowns?
options: They protect the tooth and maintain space until permanent eruption
questions.explanation: 🦅 Sami explains: 'Pediatric crowns (preformed or aesthetic) are essential to preserve function and space.' 🐆 Mina: 'Sami, you've become a specialist!'

questions.question: 🐆 Mina, seeing a child with a malocclusion, says: 'We need to monitor.' 🦅 Sami replies: 'No, we need to treat immediately.' What is the recommended approach for malocclusions in children?
options: Monitoring until complete eruption of permanent teeth
questions.explanation: 🐆 Mina explains: 'Some malocclusions correct spontaneously with growth.' 🦅 Sami: 'I prefer to treat immediately, but you're right about the principle.'

questions.question: 🦅 Sami, seeing a child with a baby tooth that hasn't come out, says: 'It's agenesis.' 🐆 Mina replies: 'Not necessarily, it could be an impaction.' What is a dental impaction?
options: A tooth that cannot erupt because it is blocked in the bone
questions.explanation: 🦅 Sami explains: 'Impaction is a blockage of eruption, often due to a positional anomaly.' 🐆 Mina: 'Sami, you know eruption anomalies well!'

questions.question: 🐆 Mina, seeing a child with a supernumerary tooth, says: 'We need to extract it.' 🦅 Sami replies: 'We can keep it.' What is a supernumerary tooth?
options: An extra tooth in the dental arch
questions.explanation: 🐆 Mina explains: 'Supernumerary teeth can cause eruption and alignment problems.' 🦅 Sami: 'I prefer to keep it, but you're right.'

questions.question: 🦅 Sami, seeing a child with a shape anomaly of teeth, says: 'It's genetic.' 🐆 Mina replies: 'Often, but not always.' What are the causes of dental anomalies?
questions.explanation: 🦅 Sami explains: 'The causes are multiple and often multifactorial.' 🐆 Mina: 'Sami, you are really up to date!'

questions.question: 🦅 Sami and 🐆 Mina discuss the future of pedodontics. Sami says: 'Teledentistry will revolutionize care!' Mina replies: 'Human contact remains essential.' What is the future of pedodontics?
options: Teledentistry complements care, but contact with the child is irreplaceable
questions.explanation: 🐆 Mina explains: 'Teledentistry is a complementary tool, but the trusting relationship with the child is paramount.' 🦅 Sami: 'I agree, we keep our jobs!'
